description: A cosy colouring book for adults: forty village corners, from a railway halt to a midnight bakery, each with a small piece of magic to find.
lead: A cosy colouring book with forty village corners, each hiding a small piece of magic to find and colour.
for: For anyone who loves cosy villages, gardens and country lanes
For colourers who like a little hidden surprise
For slow evenings and rainy Sunday afternoons

problem.h: Everyday life can feel a bit ordinary
p: Same commute, same washing, same dinner. Some weeks it’s hard to notice anything lovely at all.
And winding down at the end of the day often means a screen, which never quite does the job.

approach.h: Look closer. There’s magic in the detail.
p: Each page is a cosy corner of a village: a railway halt, a midnight bakery, a bicycle by the gate, a beekeeper’s garden, a knitting corner. And in every one, something small is misbehaving: a luggage tag floating off, a loaf rising a little too high.
Colour slowly, find the magic, and let the day go.

offer.p: Detailed, cosy line art with a little wonder on every page.

Every scene hides a small, gentle bit of magic.

proof.p: These are the actual line drawings, straight from the printed book.
note: I love the idea that ordinary things might be quietly up to something when nobody’s looking. Each page has a little piece of that.
Every picture is printed on its own page, so you can colour with pens or pencils.

decision.h: One book, forty little pieces of magic
points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: What is the “magic” in each picture?
Something small and gentle that isn’t quite ordinary, like a loaf rising too high or a tag floating away. Finding it is part of the fun.
Yes, it’s designed for adults, with fine detail. Older children who love detailed colouring may enjoy it too.
Colouring pencils give the softest results. Gel pens and fine liners are lovely for small details.
How is it different from my other colouring books?
A Cup of Somewhere Else is cosy places to escape to, and Just One More Chapter is all about books. This one is village life with a touch of magic.
